title: Incremental Feature-Flag Rollout and JIT Kernel Switch Playbook for LLM Runtime
author: Maya Chen
content:
Summary:
This playbook describes a standardized, low-risk pattern for rolling out LLM runtime changes that depend on two orthogonal controls: feature flags (logical behavior toggles) and Just-In-Time (JIT) kernel switching (binary/driver-level execution paths used by the serving runtime). The goal is to enable fast experimentation and safe progressive exposure with clear observability and rollback procedures.

Scope and audience:
- Audience: platform operators, runtime engineers, SREs, and release coordinators.
- Applies to: runtime behavior changes that are gated by both a runtime feature flag and a kernel selection (e.g., attention kernel v1 -> v2, quantized path enablement, KV-cache packing changes).
- Out of scope: model weight changes, customer contract changes, or hardware firmware upgrades (use separate runbooks).

Goals and success criteria:
- Zero-severity incidents attributable to rollout (critical incidents avoided).
- Detect regressions within 5 minutes of first production exposure.
- Ability to fully revert to previous kernel and feature flag within 3 minutes of decision.

Owner and escalation:
- Primary owner: Runtime Release Lead (oncall: runtime-release@redwood.internal)
- SRE escalation: Eng SRE Pager (pager duty) -> Page to runtime-team on-call if degradation persists >15 minutes.
- Communication owner: Release coordinator (updates #platform-releases Slack channel and incident bridge).

Prerequisites (preflight checklist):
1) Canary harness available in target region with synthetic traffic profile (tokens/s, avg seq length, prompt distribution).
2) Automated canary smoke tests passing in staging for kernel + flag combo (see test-cases matrix below).
3) Observability dashboard exists and is linked to the release ticket.
4) Fallback artifacts validated: previous kernel binaries, rollback images, and feature-flag kill switch created.
5) Stakeholders notified (Security, Customer Success if high-risk customers present).

Quick glossary:
- Feature flag: Logical toggle at RPC layer (e.g., enable_prefetch=true).
- Kernel: Binary/runtime implementation chosen at process startup or dynamically via JIT dispatcher (e.g., kernel_attention_v2).
- JIT kernel switch: Mechanism to swap execution path without full service restart (when supported).
- Canary: small percentage of traffic/tenants targeted for early exposure.

Configuration table (examples):
| Config key | Type | Typical values | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| runtime.feature_prefetch | boolean | true / false | Prefetch-related precomputation path |
| runtime.kernel_selector | enum | kernel_attention_v1, kernel_attention_v2, kernel_attention_packed | JIT kernel identifier |
| rollout.canary_pct | int | 1, 5, 10, 25 | Percent of traffic redirected to new combo |
| rollout.priority_tenants | list | [tenant-a, tenant-b] | Named tenants for priority early exposure |
Safety gates and SLO checks (automated):
- Latency P90 for generate endpoint must stay within +15% of baseline over a 5-minute sliding window.
- Error rate (5xx or model runtime errors) must be < 0.5% absolute increase over baseline in the same window.
- Token throughput variance should be within historical mean +/- 20% for synthetic driver.
- Model-output quality smoke checks: hallucination score and f1 for small eval set must not degrade by >3%.

Automated monitors to create if missing:
1) Canary pulse monitor (5m): tracks P50/P90/P99 latency, sparklines vs baseline.
2) Error funnel alert (1m): 5xx or runtime_exceptions spike > 0.5% -> Pager.
3) Quality regression alarm (15m): eval harness regression > threshold -> Notify but no immediate pager.
4) Kernel health heartbeat: process-level metric for kernel init failures and OOMs.

Step-by-step rollout procedure (operators):
Pre-rollout (run 1 hour before):
- (A) Create Release ticket in Jira with exact binary & flag versions. Attach dashboards and list of fast responders.
- (B) Confirm rollback images/artifacts exist in artifact registry and are tagged.
- (C) Warm up synthetic canary node(s) with 10 minutes of traffic to ensure warm KV caches.

Stage 0: Local smoke (non-prod)
1. Deploy kernel change to staging runtime and enable feature flag using local toggles.
2. Run full smoke suite and lightweight evals (10–20 prompts). All checks must pass.

Stage 1: Canary customers / priority tenants (1–5% traffic)
1. Set rollout.canary_pct=1 and add priority_tenants list to include 2–3 known low-risk tenants.
2. Flip feature flag for canary environment only.
3. Observe metrics for 10 minutes: if meets safety gates, increase to 5%.
4. On every increment (1 -> 5 -> 10) run the quick regression harness (10m) and confirm quality alarms clear.

Stage 2: Regional ramp and JIT kernel switch (10–25%)
1. If runtime supports JIT kernel switching, schedule a 1-minute maintenance window in the region.
2. Perform JIT kernel switch on one canary node using the operator CLI:
   - CLI example:
     redwood-runtimectl --region us-west2 canary switch-kernel --node id=<node-id> --kernel kernel_attention_v2
3. Confirm node-level health metrics: kernel_init_success=1, kernel_latency_ratio ~ baseline.
4. If nodes are healthy after 5 minutes, apply to remaining canary nodes then increase canary_pct to 25%.

Stage 3: Broad rollout (25% -> 100%)
1. Use a staged percentage schedule (25%, 50%, 75%, 100%) with at least 15 minutes of stable observation at each step.
2. Maintain the ability to toggle the feature flag instantly for all traffic. Kernel-level rollback can be slower; prefer flag-first rollback.

Rollback decision matrix (fast vs safe):
- Fast rollback (immediate): triggered on error rate spike >1% absolute or any critical customer-impacting error. Action: flip feature flag global=false, notify stakeholders, retain kernel for forensic capture.
- Safe rollback (investigate): small latency regression but no errors: pause rollout, run deeper profiling for 30 minutes, then either continue or flip flag.
- Kernel-level rollback: if JIT-revertable, revert kernels on canary nodes first; if not revertable without restart, flip feature flag to route new requests to fallback path and schedule rolling restart with fallback image.

Operator commands and snippets:
- list canary nodes:
  redwood-runtimectl --region us-east1 canary list --filter kernel!=kernel_attention_v2
- flip flag for tenant(s):
  redwood-ffctl set runtime.feature_prefetch=false --tenants tenant-a,tenant-b --reason "rollback due to latency"
- force kernel revert (non-JIT):
  deploy-tool rollback-image --service runtime --image redwood/runtime:20260112-prev

Observability dashboard template (sections to include):
- Canary overview panel: canary_pct, canary_tenants, active_kernel_id, feature_flag_state
- Latency panels: P50/P90/P99 absolute + diff vs baseline, split by tenant class
- Error panels: 5xx rate, rpc_exceptions, kernel_init_errors
- Resource panels: GPU utilization, memory/backing-store OOMs, kernel-specific GPU kernels time
- Quality panels: eval_hallucination_score, sample_f1, perplexity_on_eval_set

Failure modes and runbook actions:
1) Kernel init failures on startup:
   - Action: Identify failing node via kernel_init_errors. If initial failure rate >10% across canary nodes, abort rollout and mark for image rollback.
2) Gradual latency creep without error spike:
   - Action: Pause rollout, capture perf traces (per-node trace), compare kernel-level op times, engage runtime devs. Consider turning off prefetch/async paths.
3) Silent quality regression (no metric spike but downstream eval degrades):
   - Action: Immediately reduce canary_pct to 0, retain logs/trace, run full eval harness and create incident if confirmed.
4) High-severity crash (OOM or segfault):
   - Action: Pager to on-call SRE, flip feature flag, evacuate affected nodes, schedule rolling restart with previous kernel if recoverable.

Post-rollout retrospective template (to fill in after any non-trivial rollout):
- Rollout ID / ticket:
- Dates and times: start / detection / rollback / full-rollout
- Owners present:
- What went well:
- What failed / surprising observations:
- Root cause (if any):
- Action items and owners (with due dates):

Testing matrix (minimal):
| Test | Target environment | Expected pass criteria |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Unit perf smoke | local | kernel_init success, no regressions >10% in hot-path microbench |
| Staging functional | staging | API responses match golden set (100% match for structured outputs) |
| Canary synthetic | canary nodes | P90 latency within +15%, error rate <0.5%
| Quality regression | canary eval harness | hallucination delta <3% and f1 delta <3% |

Schedule and runway guidance:
- For low-risk kernel patches (minor perf optimizations): 2–6 hours from canary start to full rollout with continuous monitoring.
- For high-risk changes (quantization changes, memory layout): 24–72 hour runway with manual approvals at 5%/25%/75% milestones.

Communication checklist (on release day):
- Pre-rollout message in #platform-releases with links to dashboards and rollback controls.
- Hourly updates during broad rollout or on any escalation.
- Post-rollout summary with metrics and any action items.
